newsitem.title: UK: UK retail prices rise yr/yr 2.1 pct in August.
newsitem.headline: UK retail prices rise yr/yr 2.1 pct in August.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics released the following August retail price indices.
RETAIL PRICES INDEX AUGUST JULY AUG 95
Mth pct change ex MIPs, tax 0.7 -0.5 0.6
COMPONENT DETAILS OF THE ALL-ITEMS INDEX (PCT CHANGES) -
NOTE - Consensus forecast was RPI +0.4 pct month-on-month and +2.1 pct YY, RPIX +2.7 pct YY, RPIY +2.3 pct YY.

The ONS said seasonal food prices made the major contribution to the fall in the 12-month headline rate of inflation. Other significant downward pressures were exerted by housing costs, prices for personal goods and charges for leisure services. The main upward pressure came from motoring costs.

The 5.3 percent rise in August seasonal food prices compares with an exceptionally large, 13.1 percent increase in August last year. Prices for fresh vegetables continued to fall, contrasting with the unusual rise last year, triggered by a prolonged spell of dry weather.
In non-seasonal food, there was upward pressure from beef as prices returned to more normal levels in August, after July's reductions, the ONS said.

A 1.0 percent monthly increase in motoring expenditure contrasted with a 0.3 percent drop last year. There was upward pressure from a sharp rise in petrol and oil prices as opposed to small reductions in August last year. Rising consumer demand for motor vehicles also pushed prices up in that sector.
Outlook for September RPl: The ONS noted that seasonal food prices normally fall in September, while supermarket price wars would also exert downward pressure.

Housing costs are expected to fall further because of the continued drop in mortgage rates, while a five percent increase in private education fees may have an effect on household service, the ONS added. British Telecommunications is expected to cut the price of certain telephone calls, it said.
